title.narrative: Increased capacities for gender equality and equal opportunities and treatment for all in the world of work

description.narrative:
Namibia continues to promote gender equality, non-discrimination and inclusion in the world of work as part of its national, regional and international commitments to social justice and decent work. The country has made progress through legislative reforms, ratification of key ILO Conventions and the integration of gender equality, HIV and AIDS, disability, non-discrimination, violence and harassment at work and the promotion of decent work for domestic workers and workplace rights into national policies.
However, persistent challenges remain, including gender inequalities in labour market participation, wage gaps, occupational segregation, and limited representation of women in decision-making roles, particularly in key sectors of the economy. The disproportionate burden of unpaid care and domestic work continues to constrain women’s economic participation, while violence and harassment in the world of work, including gender-based violence, and HIV-related stigma and discrimination remain concerns in certain workplaces and sectors.
The ILO supports Namibia to advance gender equality, non-discrimination and inclusion in the world of work in line with these commitments. The interventions focus on promoting equal opportunities and treatment for women and men, addressing structural inequalities, and strengthening the prevention and elimination of violence and harassment at work, including through the implementation of Convention No. 190. Attention is given to domestic workers, workers with family responsibilities, the recognition and redistribution of care work, and the strengthening of workplace responses to HIV and AIDS, especially for workers in vulnerable situations.
The strategy includes policy support, research, awareness raising, capacity building and tripartite dialogue, evidence-based research on the care economy and advocacy for equality and inclusion to contribute to safe, inclusive and equitable workplaces across Namibia’s economy.
